## Overview

Dune: Imperium is a deck-building worker-placement game. Each player leads a Great House of the Landsraad: you play cards to send Agents to board spaces, use Persuasion to acquire new cards for your deck, recruit and deploy troops to fight over each round's Conflict card, and climb the Influence tracks of four Factions (Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen), earning Alliances. Successes are measured in Victory Points. At the end of any round in which a player has reached 10 or more VP (or the Conflict Deck is empty), the game ends and whoever has the most Victory Points wins.

Each Leader has two unique abilities: one used during play as described on the Leader, and a Signet Ring ability activated when you play your Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns. Note: cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.

**Scope:** original 2020 Dune: Imperium base game, standard 2–4-player multiplayer. Two-player play requires one House Hagal Rival (see below). Solo play, optional variants, expansions and Dune: Imperium — Uprising rules are excluded. Clarifications incorporate the official January 13, 2025 FAQ where applicable to this base game.

## Components

- Game board
- 8 Leaders (two each from four Great Houses), with a Turn Sequence guide on their backs. Leaders have 1-3 icons after their names; more icons = more strategically complex.
- 67 Imperium Deck cards
- 24 Reserve cards: 8 Arrakis Liaison, 10 The Spice Must Flow, 6 Foldspace
- 40 Intrigue cards
- 18 Conflict cards: 4 Conflict I, 10 Conflict II, 4 Conflict III
- Solari tokens: 4 large (worth 5), 20 small (worth 1)
- Spice tokens: 3 large (worth 5), 20 small (worth 1)
- 15 water tokens
- 4 Alliance tokens, First Player marker, Mentat (a freelance Agent pawn)
- 4 Baron Harkonnen tokens (used only with the Baron Vladimir Harkonnen Leader)
- Board Space Guide sheet; House Hagal rules sheet and 31 House Hagal cards (used only in solo and two-player games)
- Per player, in their color: 3 Agents, 3 Control markers, 1 Combat marker, a 10-card starting deck, 16 cubes (4 become Influence markers; the other 12 are your troops), 2 discs — 1 Score marker and 1 Councilor token

**Starting deck (10 cards, identical for all players):** Convincing Argument x2, Dagger x2, Dune the Desert Planet x2, Diplomacy, Reconnaissance, Seek Allies, Signet Ring.

## Setup

1. Place the game board. Place the Mentat on its side in the Mentat space, and the 4 Alliance tokens on the marked areas of the four Factions' Influence tracks.
2. Build the face-down 10-card Conflict Deck using **three separately shuffled tiers**. Its final order from **top to bottom** is: **1 card randomly dealt from the shuffled 4 Conflict I cards; 5 cards randomly dealt from the shuffled 10 Conflict II cards; all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order**. Shuffle every tier before taking its cards. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
3. Along the board edge: shuffle the Intrigue Deck and place it face down. Shuffle the Imperium Deck, place it face down, and deal 5 cards face up from it to form the Imperium Row. Place the Reserve cards in three stacks: Arrakis Liaison, The Spice Must Flow, and Foldspace.
4. Each player takes a Leader (chosen or random) and all components of one color. First-game recommendation: everyone uses a one-icon Leader (Paul Atreides, Glossu "The Beast" Rabban, Earl Memnon Thorvald, or Count Ilban Richese).
5. Each player places 2 Agents on their Leader and sets their third Agent (their Swordmaster) next to the game board. Shuffle your 10-card starting deck and place it face down in your supply, to the left of your Leader.
6. Each player places one of their two discs on the Score track: on the **1** space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the **0** space. Place your Combat marker (correct side face up) on the 0 space of the Combat track.
7. Each player places 4 cubes, one each, on the bottom spaces of the four Factions' Influence tracks. The other 12 cubes are your troops: place 3 in the circular garrison on the board closest to you, and the rest in your supply along with your remaining components, in clear view of all players.
8. Each player takes 1 water. Create a bank next to the board with the Solari, spice, and remaining water tokens (these are not limited; substitute if you run out).
9. Randomly determine a first player, who takes the First Player marker. For two-player play, also set up House Hagal as described below.

## Turn Structure

The game is played in rounds, each with five phases in this order: **1. Round Start, 2. Player Turns, 3. Combat, 4. Makers, 5. Recall.**

### Phase 1: Round Start
- Reveal a new Conflict card from the top of the Conflict Deck and place it face up next to the deck (on top of Conflict cards from previous rounds).
- Each player draws 5 cards from their own deck to form their hand for the round.

### Phase 2: Player Turns
Starting with the holder of the First Player marker and continuing clockwise, players take **one turn at a time**. On your turn, take either an **Agent turn** or a **Reveal turn**. Generally you take Agent turns until you run out of Agents, then take a Reveal turn — but Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left. Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase; the phase ends when all players have taken a Reveal turn.

You may play Plot Intrigue cards during this phase, at any point during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

**Agent turn** — play one card from your hand face up, using it to send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied board space:
- The board space must show (in its upper-left corner) an icon matching one of the Agent icons on the card. You must choose only one Agent icon on the card; one card can't send multiple Agents. A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn — it can only be revealed during a Reveal turn.
- You can't send an Agent to a board space that already has an Agent on it.
- You must pay any costs and meet any requirements of the space. Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card; if you can't pay, you can't send your Agent there.
- Gain the effects of the board space, the card's **Agent box**, and the one-space Influence advancement for a Faction space **in any order**, after paying the entry cost (ignore the card's Reveal box).
- Arrows mean cost (left of / above the arrow) then effect (right of / below it). An optional arrow effect can be paid and resolved **once**, never repeated by paying again. You may decline the payment and its effect on an ordinary card; board entry costs must be paid to enter, and an Intrigue card's costs and conditions must be met to play it. Most other board/card effects are mandatory unless they say “may,” use an optional arrow, or use the optional black-X trash icon. A non-arrow instruction to trash the card itself is mandatory.
- **Recruiting:** each troop icon recruits one troop — take it from your supply and place it in your garrison. (If your supply is out of troops, you can't recruit more until some return.)
- **Deploying:** troops sitting in your garrison can't earn rewards. Only when you send an Agent to a **Combat space** may you deploy troops to the Conflict area (the center of the garrisons): any or all troops you recruited this turn (from any source, including the board space, played card and Intrigue cards), **plus up to two more troops from your garrison**. You cannot re-recruit garrison troops to evade that limit. Recruited troops you don't deploy go to your garrison as usual.

**Reveal turn** — taken when you have no Agents left (or choose not to use remaining Agents). Four steps, in order:
1. **Reveal Cards:** reveal all cards remaining in your hand, face up, kept separate from cards you played on Agent turns.
2. **Resolve Reveal Effects:** gain the effects in the **Reveal boxes** of the cards you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round), in any order. A card drawn during your Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used in that turn; it cannot become an Agent turn. Cards drawn after your Reveal turn stay in your hand for next round, when you still draw five additional cards. You may spend Persuasion to acquire new cards before, between, or after your Reveal effects (see Actions).
3. **Set Strength:** total your strength for this round's Combat — each of your troops in the Conflict is worth **2 strength**; each sword you revealed during your Reveal turn is worth **1 strength**. Troops in your garrison or supply contribute nothing. You must have at least one troop in the Conflict to have any strength: if your last troop is ever removed, your strength becomes 0 and can't be increased by any means, including swords. Announce your total and move your Combat marker to that space of the Combat track (if over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track).
4. **Clean Up:** put all the cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) into your discard pile.

Note: a Reveal turn has no troop-deployment step. Deployment happens on Agent turns at Combat spaces (or via specific card/Control effects).

### Phase 3: Combat
- **Combat Intrigue cards:** starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player **with at least one troop in the Conflict** may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards, or pass. You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase. Once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, resolve the Combat. If a card changes a player's troops in the Conflict (or otherwise alters strength), adjust their Combat marker — remember, with no troops in the Conflict your strength is 0. A few Combat Intrigue cards trigger "when you win a Conflict": play those only after you've won, before moving to the next phase.
- **Resolve Combat:** rewards from the Conflict card are given by strength as shown on the Combat track. Highest strength wins the Conflict and gains the top reward; second-highest gains the second reward; **in a 4-player game only**, an ordinary third-place finisher gains the third reward. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
- **Ties:** tied for first place — no one wins the Conflict; each tied player receives the **second** reward (in a 4-player game, if two players tie for first, the other two still compete for the third reward). Tied for second — each receives the third reward, **including in two- and three-player games**; this differs from an ordinary third-place finish. Tied for third — nothing. “When you win a Conflict” effects cannot be used on a first-place tie because nobody won. If a win-trigger Intrigue is itself drawn as a victory reward, you may play it immediately.
- Once all rewards are given, each player takes their troops from the Conflict and puts them in their **supply (not their garrison)**. Reset all Combat markers to 0.

### Phase 4: Makers

If a card shows two spaces, use only the option matching the current conditions: if that option is occupied, draw a new card, never switch to the other option. Immediately reshuffle the House Hagal cards if the deck is empty or the Reshuffle card appears; continue revealing as needed.

Ignore the normal costs, requirements and effects of the space. Resolve only the revealed card’s icons and instructions. Influence icons advance its cube; it receives no Influence-track bonuses but takes an Alliance if able. Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play (they are solo-only). Any time it sends an Agent to a Combat space, **also deploy up to two garrison troops**, even if the card recruited none. **Combat strength procedure:** if House Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, calculate its strength at the start of Combat:
1. Reveal a House Hagal card in turn order. **If it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again**; obtain a card with a combat sword bonus before calculating that bonus. A Reshuffle result is not treated as a zero-sword combat card.
2. Ignore everything except the sword icons at the bottom; add that many strength to its normal **2 strength per deployed troop**.
3. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue cards before resolving Combat.

House Hagal receives no reward for its rank, but it still occupies that rank when humans receive rewards. Ordinary third place pays nothing; a tie for second pays the third reward to each tied human. If House Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker; House Hagal does not replace it. After Combat, troops return to supply and markers reset normally.

## FAQ & Rulings

These clarifications apply to the original base game; expansions, promo additions and Uprising-specific clauses of the shared FAQ are excluded.

- **Mentat reward:** for Sort Through the Chaos, take the Mentat **at the start of the next round**. It is available as an Agent that round.
- **Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy:** Assassination Mission provides no way to trash itself for its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws an Intrigue only when you use its own self-trash effect, not when another effect trashes it.
- **The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers:** keep the VP gained for acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if you later trash it. Guild Bankers’ discount applies to **each** copy you acquire that turn.
- **Corner the Market:** count The Spice Must Flow cards in your deck and discard pile. Compare each opponent separately; if any one has at least as many as you, you do not meet the card’s second requirement.
- **Count Ilban Richese / Countess Ariana Thorvald:** Ruthless Negotiator triggers only for paying the printed Solari cost of a board space, not a card ability costing Solari. Ariana’s Spice Addict is mandatory and affects only spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice gained by other means.
- **Carryall / Liet Kynes:** original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin and 3 at The Great Flat; accumulated bonus spice is not base spice. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from your Agent turns this round and your current Reveal turn, providing 2 Persuasion for each.
- **Helena Richese — Manipulate:** opponents cannot acquire the card you set aside. You may acquire it by another effect, but its 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If you have not acquired it by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
- **Dispatch an Envoy:** it adds only missing Faction Agent icons. Existing icons remain, including non-Faction icons; it never creates a duplicate icon.
- **Double Cross / Gun Thopter:** Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but does not require a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter’s Agent box does not affect an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
- **Shifting Allegiances:** you may lose and gain Influence with the same Faction for a net gain of one. You must actually pay the one-Influence loss; a Faction where you have zero cannot pay it.
- **Recruitment Mission:** its acquisition destination choice applies only during your Reveal turn that round, not Agent-turn acquisitions. Choose independently for each card acquired whether it goes atop your deck or into your discard pile.
- **Refocus / Poison Snooper:** Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. Cards drawn during a Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used during that turn.
- **Missionaria Protectiva erratum:** it belongs to the Bene Gesserit Faction; that label is missing in the first English printing. After replacing misprints, include only two copies in the Imperium deck.


## Player Reference

**Round:** 1. Round Start (reveal Conflict card; draw 5) → 2. Player Turns (Agent turns, then your Reveal turn) → 3. Combat → 4. Makers (1 bonus spice on each Agent-free Maker space) → 5. Recall (check 10 VP / empty Conflict Deck; return Mentat; recall Agents; pass First Player marker).

**Agent turn:** play 1 card with a matching icon → send 1 Agent to an unoccupied space → pay costs first → resolve space + Agent box in any order (+1 Influence at Faction spaces) → at a Combat space, may deploy this turn's recruits + up to 2 garrison troops.

**Reveal turn:** reveal remaining hand → resolve Reveal boxes + spend Persuasion on cards → set strength → discard all cards in play. (No troop deployment on a Reveal turn.)

**Strength:** troop in the Conflict = 2; revealed sword = 1; no troops in the Conflict = 0, no matter what.

**Combat rewards:** 1st = top reward, 2nd = second, 3rd = third (4-player games only); 0 strength = nothing. First-place tie: no winner, tied players take the second reward. Second-place tie: third reward each even in two- or three-player games. Third-place tie: nothing. Troops then return to **supply**; Combat markers to 0.

**Influence:** 2 = 1 VP (lost if you drop below); 4 = track bonus (kept) + Alliance token for the first player there (transfers if someone rises higher).

**Costs:** Conspire 4 spice · Heighliner 6 spice · Selective Breeding 2 spice · Hardy Warriors 1 water · Hagga Basin 1 water · The Great Flat 2 water · Research Station 2 water · Sell Melange 2-5 spice · Rally Troops 4 Solari · High Council 5 Solari (once/game) · Swordmaster 8 Solari (once/game) · Mentat 2 Solari · Sietch Tabr requires 2+ Fremen Influence.

**Game end:** at end of round with any player at 10+ VP, or Conflict Deck empty → Endgame Intrigue cards → most VP wins. Ties: spice → Solari → water → garrisoned troops → most recent Reveal turn.

**Starting deck (10):** Convincing Argument x2, Dagger x2, Dune the Desert Planet x2, Diplomacy, Reconnaissance, Seek Allies, Signet Ring.

## Actions

### Agent icons
Seven Agent icons appear on cards and board spaces: **Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen, Landsraad, City, Spice Trade**. A card's icons determine where it can send your Agent — e.g., Sardaukar Legion's Emperor icon reaches either of the two Emperor spaces, while its Landsraad icon instead reaches one of the five Landsraad board spaces (the Mentat's designated space is in the Landsraad). Each Faction has one board space with a cost and one without.

### Board spaces
Sending an Agent to a Faction's space also gains 1 Influence with that Faction (included below).

| Space | Faction icon | Cost / Requirement | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wealth | Emperor | — | +1 Emperor Influence; gain 2 Solari |
| Conspire | Emperor | 4 spice | +1 Emperor Influence; gain 5 Solari, recruit 2 troops, draw an Intrigue card |
| Foldspace | Spacing Guild | — | +1 Spacing Guild Influence; acquire a Foldspace card from the Reserve |
| Heighliner | Spacing Guild | 6 spice | +1 Spacing Guild Influence; recruit 5 troops and gain 2 water |
| Secrets | Bene Gesserit | — | +1 Bene Gesserit Influence; draw an Intrigue card; each opponent with 4+ Intrigue cards gives you one (selected at random) |
| Selective Breeding | Bene Gesserit | 2 spice | +1 Bene Gesserit Influence; trash one card to draw two cards |
| Stillsuits | Fremen | — | +1 Fremen Influence; gain 1 water |
| Hardy Warriors | Fremen | 1 water | +1 Fremen Influence; recruit 2 troops |
| Arrakeen | — | — | Recruit a troop and draw a card. Arrakeen's controller gains 1 Solari |
| Carthag | — | — | Recruit a troop and draw an Intrigue card. Carthag's controller gains 1 Solari |
| Sietch Tabr | — | Requires 2+ Fremen Influence | Recruit a troop and gain 1 water |
| Research Station | — | 2 water | Draw three cards |

| Hagga Basin | — | 1 water | Gain 2 spice, plus any bonus spice |

| Secure Contract | — | — | Gain 3 Solari |
| Sell Melange | — | 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 spice | Gain 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 Solari, respectively; one exchange per turn |
| High Council | — | 5 Solari | Once per game only: place your Councilor token on an unoccupied Council seat; for the rest of the game, gain 2 Persuasion during each of your Reveal turns |
| Swordmaster | — | 8 Solari | Once per game only: gain your Swordmaster (your third Agent) and place it on your Leader; you have three Agents for the rest of the game, including this round |
| Hall of Oratory | — | — | Recruit a troop. During your Reveal turn, gain 1 Persuasion if you have an Agent here |

The **City** spaces are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr and Research Station. The **Spice Trade** spaces are Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Secure Contract and Sell Melange. The **Landsraad** spaces are High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops and Mentat.

The complete list of **Combat spaces** is: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors and Stillsuits. Each has a desert illustration and crossed swords. Other spaces, including Conspire and Rally Troops, do not normally allow deployment.

### Acquiring cards
Persuasion gained during a round is used during your **Reveal turn** to acquire new cards: any of the five cards in the Imperium Row, or Arrakis Liaison or The Spice Must Flow from the Reserve. (Foldspace requires an acquire-Foldspace icon, normally from the Foldspace board space; it cannot be bought with Persuasion.) A card's cost is shown at its top right. Acquire as many cards as you can afford; you may pool Persuasion from multiple sources (cards and board spaces) for one card, and may split Persuasion from a single source across different cards. Persuasion can never be saved — whatever you don't use during your Reveal turn is lost. Acquired cards go to your discard pile (face up, to the right of your Leader); you don't use them right away. The Imperium Row must always have five cards: refill it immediately from the Imperium Deck, so after acquiring a card you may also acquire its replacement if you can afford it. Some cards have an **Acquire box** beneath their cost: gain that effect one time, at the moment you acquire the card (not later when you play it).

### Trashing cards
A direction to **discard** means a card from your hand unless otherwise specified; it goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card — from your hand, your discard pile, or in play — to the game box for the rest of the game (Reserve cards are returned to their Reserve stack instead). Trashing is optional unless it's paying a cost or a card directs you to trash itself.

### Intrigue cards
Intrigue cards can provide resources, Influence, or even Victory Points. You receive them primarily from three board spaces — Carthag, Conspire, and Secrets — plus card effects showing the Intrigue card icon. Keep them face down, separate from your deck; you may look at them at any time and reveal them only when played. After a played Intrigue card resolves, discard it face up next to the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue deck is exhausted, shuffle its discards into a new deck. A Plot card whose effect applies at your next Reveal turn (such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission) can be played on your Agent turn: leave it face up until that Reveal turn, use it then, and discard it. Three types:
- **Plot** — play any time during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.
- **Combat** — play only during Combat.
- **Endgame** — play only at the end of the game.

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

- Whenever you gain or lose a Victory Point, move your Score marker up or down one space on the Score track.
- **Game end trigger:** at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall), if any player has reached **10 or more Victory Points**, or the **Conflict Deck is empty**, the game ends.
- **Endgame:** first, players may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards they have. Then whoever has the most Victory Points is declared the winner.
- **Tiebreakers, in order:** amount of **spice**, then **Solari**, then **water**, then **garrisoned troops** (troops in your garrison on the board — not troops in your supply), then the player who **most recently took a Reveal turn**. You can score above 12 VP; the end of the printed Score track is not a limit.
- **VP sources include:** Conflict card rewards; reaching 2 Influence with a Faction (1 VP each — lost again if you drop back below 2); Alliance tokens (worth the VP shown on the token, and transferable — see below); and card effects, notably Intrigue cards (including Endgame Intrigue at game end).

## Special Rules & Edge Cases

- **Faction Influence:** your cube starts at the bottom of each track. Sending an Agent to a Faction's board space gains 1 Influence with that Faction; other effects can move you up (or occasionally down). At **2 Influence** you gain a VP (lost if you drop below 2, regained if you reach 2 again). Each track has six spaces; 3 Influence is the space immediately above the 2-Influence VP space. At **4 Influence** you earn the bonus shown on that space of the track; you do *not* give the bonus back if you later drop below 4, and you can even earn it again by dropping back and re-advancing.
- **Alliances:** the **first** player to reach 4 Influence with a Faction takes its Alliance token and gains the VP shown on it. If an opponent ever passes them by rising to a **higher** space on that track, the token (and its VP) transfers to that opponent. Merely tying the holder does not take it. If the holder loses Influence while previously tied with another player, the previously tied player takes it; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. The holder also loses the token if falling to 3 Influence or less: if no player has 4 or more to take it, return it to the board. Every Alliance ownership change immediately moves **both** affected scores: the former holder loses its 1 VP and the new holder gains 1 VP; returning it to the board just loses the former holder's VP.
- **Mentat:** a freelance Agent. Take it only from its space on the board (you can't take it from another player or another space), place it on your Leader, and use it as one of your Agents this round; return it to its Landsraad space during Recall. For the Sort Through the Chaos Conflict reward, take the Mentat at the start of the next round and use it that round (official FAQ timing).
- **Swordmaster & High Council** are once-per-game spaces for each player (8 Solari for your third Agent; 5 Solari for a Council seat granting 2 Persuasion every Reveal turn).
- **Control:** some Conflict cards (titled for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin) reward control of that space. If you win such a Conflict, place a Control marker on the flag below that space (replacing any opponent's marker). While it's there, you receive the bonus whenever **any** player, including yourself, sends an Agent there: 1 Solari for Arrakeen or Carthag, 1 spice for Imperial Basin. **Defensive bonus:** when a Conflict card is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop **from your supply** to the Conflict.
- **Deck exhaustion:** any time you're unable to draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile to form a new deck, then continue drawing. You can't reshuffle early — e.g., Paul Atreides' ability or Poison Snooper can't look at the top card of an empty deck.
- **Recall effects:** return the recalled Agent to your Leader; you may use it on another Agent turn in the same round. This does not reopen turns after your Reveal turn.
- **Losing vs. retreating troops:** a **lost** troop returns to your supply (not your garrison); a **retreated** troop moves from the Conflict back to your garrison. If an effect permits retreating “any number,” zero is allowed.
- **In play / Fremen Bond:** cards you play on Agent turns and reveal on your Reveal turn stay face up "in play" until your Clean Up (unless trashed first). Fremen Bond effects work if you have at least one *other* Fremen card in play; two Fremen Bond cards activate one another regardless of the order played.
- **Conditional icons:** Alliance-icon effects require holding that Faction's Alliance token; Influence-requirement icons need at least the shown Influence with that Faction. "Gain two Influence" effects can't be split between two Factions.
- **Steal Intrigue:** each opponent with four or more Intrigue cards must give you one, selected at random.
- **Rulebook clarifications:**
  - *Bindu Suspension:* play at the start of your Agent turn, before anything else; draw a card, then immediately end your turn.
  - *Calculated Hire:* can only take the Mentat from its starting position in the Landsraad.
  - *Demand Respect:* if you win a Conflict that rewards spice, you may take that spice first and use it to play this card (To the Victor… can likewise fund it).
  - *Kwisatz Haderach:* lets you take an Agent turn with no Agents left by sending an Agent already on a board space (even back to the same space). It can't reuse once-per-game spaces (High Council, Swordmaster) and can't overcome The Voice.
  - *Maker spaces:* if an Agent moves away from a Maker space and it's still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice does accumulate there.
  - *Test of Humanity:* opponents choose starting from your left, clockwise; each must choose something they can actually do (no discarding from an empty hand, no losing a deployed troop they don't have); a discarding opponent chooses the card — it isn't random.
  - *The Voice:* mark the chosen board space with one of your available Control markers and remove it on your next turn; it stops opponents (including via Kwisatz Haderach) from sending Agents there for one turn.
  - *Baron Vladimir Harkonnen (Masterstroke):* after completing all setup and before the first round, secretly choose two of the four Baron Harkonnen tokens and place them Faction-side down on your Leader; return the other two to the box unseen; reveal later as described to gain your reward, only once per game.
### Two-player House Hagal Rival

House Hagal is a third, spoiler Rival in every standard two-player game. It does not collect resources, build an Imperium deck, earn Conflict rewards or score VP, and cannot claim Control. It can take and hold Faction Alliances, denying their VP to humans. It is affected by effects targeting opponents or players if it has the specified resources.

**Setup:** choose an unused color. Put one of its cubes at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks; all remaining cubes go in its supply, with **no troops in its garrison**. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked “1P,” shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards and put the deck and its **three Agents** near its supply. No Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules are used.

**Agent turns:** after each of the **First Player’s Agent turns**, House Hagal takes one Agent turn if it has an Agent left in supply. It does not act after the other human’s turn or after a Reveal turn. Thus it may take three turns when the First Player has a Swordmaster and two when the next round’s First Player does not. It never takes a Reveal turn. Recall its Agents to its supply for the next round.

Reveal the top House Hagal card and send an Agent to the indicated space if unoccupied; otherwise keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If a card shows two spaces, use only the option matching the current conditions: if that option is occupied, draw a new card, never switch to the other option. Immediately reshuffle the House Hagal cards if the deck is empty or the Reshuffle card appears; continue revealing as needed.

Ignore the normal costs, requirements and effects of the space. Resolve only the revealed card’s icons and instructions. Influence icons advance its cube; it receives no Influence-track bonuses but takes an Alliance if able. Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play (they are solo-only). Each troop icon recruits a troop from its supply: deploy it if this is a Combat space, otherwise put it in its garrison. Any time it sends an Agent to a Combat space, **also deploy up to two garrison troops**, even if the card recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; remove harvested bonus spice from the space and return it to the bank, rather than accumulating resources for House Hagal.

**Combat strength procedure:** if House Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, calculate its strength at the start of Combat:
1. Reveal a House Hagal card in turn order. **If it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again**; obtain a card with a combat sword bonus before calculating that bonus. A Reshuffle result is not treated as a zero-sword combat card.
2. Ignore everything except the sword icons at the bottom; add that many strength to its normal **2 strength per deployed troop**.
3. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue cards before resolving Combat.

House Hagal receives no reward for its rank, but it still occupies that rank when humans receive rewards. Ordinary third place pays nothing; a tie for second pays the third reward to each tied human. If House Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker; House Hagal does not replace it. After Combat, troops return to supply and markers reset normally.

## FAQ & Rulings

These clarifications apply to the original base game; expansions, promo additions and Uprising-specific clauses of the shared FAQ are excluded.

- **Mentat reward:** for Sort Through the Chaos, take the Mentat **at the start of the next round**. It is available as an Agent that round.
- **Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy:** Assassination Mission provides no way to trash itself for its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws an Intrigue only when you use its own self-trash effect, not when another effect trashes it.
- **The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers:** keep the VP gained for acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if you later trash it. Guild Bankers’ discount applies to **each** copy you acquire that turn.
- **Corner the Market:** count The Spice Must Flow cards in your deck and discard pile. Compare each opponent separately; if any one has at least as many as you, you do not meet the card’s second requirement.
- **Count Ilban Richese / Countess Ariana Thorvald:** Ruthless Negotiator triggers only for paying the printed Solari cost of a board space, not a card ability costing Solari. Ariana’s Spice Addict is mandatory and affects only spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice gained by other means.
- **Carryall / Liet Kynes:** original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin and 3 at The Great Flat; accumulated bonus spice is not base spice. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from your Agent turns this round and your current Reveal turn, providing 2 Persuasion for each.
- **Helena Richese — Manipulate:** opponents cannot acquire the card you set aside. You may acquire it by another effect, but its 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If you have not acquired it by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
- **Dispatch an Envoy:** it adds only missing Faction Agent icons. Existing icons remain, including non-Faction icons; it never creates a duplicate icon.
- **Double Cross / Gun Thopter:** Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but does not require a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter’s Agent box does not affect an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
- **Shifting Allegiances:** you may lose and gain Influence with the same Faction for a net gain of one. You must actually pay the one-Influence loss; a Faction where you have zero cannot pay it.
- **Recruitment Mission:** its acquisition destination choice applies only during your Reveal turn that round, not Agent-turn acquisitions. Choose independently for each card acquired whether it goes atop your deck or into your discard pile.
- **Refocus / Poison Snooper:** Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. Cards drawn during a Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used during that turn.
- **Missionaria Protectiva erratum:** it belongs to the Bene Gesserit Faction; that label is missing in the first English printing. After replacing misprints, include only two copies in the Imperium deck.


## Player Reference

**Round:** 1. Round Start (reveal Conflict card; draw 5) → 2. Player Turns (Agent turns, then your Reveal turn) → 3. Combat → 4. Makers (1 bonus spice on each Agent-free Maker space) → 5. Recall (check 10 VP / empty Conflict Deck; return Mentat; recall Agents; pass First Player marker).

**Agent turn:** play 1 card with a matching icon → send 1 Agent to an unoccupied space → pay costs first → resolve space + Agent box in any order (+1 Influence at Faction spaces) → at a Combat space, may deploy this turn's recruits + up to 2 garrison troops.

**Reveal turn:** reveal remaining hand → resolve Reveal boxes + spend Persuasion on cards → set strength → discard all cards in play. (No troop deployment on a Reveal turn.)

**Strength:** troop in the Conflict = 2; revealed sword = 1; no troops in the Conflict = 0, no matter what.

**Combat rewards:** 1st = top reward, 2nd = second, 3rd = third (4-player games only); 0 strength = nothing. First-place tie: no winner, tied players take the second reward. Second-place tie: third reward each even in two- or three-player games. Third-place tie: nothing. Troops then return to **supply**; Combat markers to 0.

**Influence:** 2 = 1 VP (lost if you drop below); 4 = track bonus (kept) + Alliance token for the first player there (transfers if someone rises higher).

**Costs:** Conspire 4 spice · Heighliner 6 spice · Selective Breeding 2 spice · Hardy Warriors 1 water · Hagga Basin 1 water · The Great Flat 2 water · Research Station 2 water · Sell Melange 2-5 spice · Rally Troops 4 Solari · High Council 5 Solari (once/game) · Swordmaster 8 Solari (once/game) · Mentat 2 Solari · Sietch Tabr requires 2+ Fremen Influence.

**Game end:** at end of round with any player at 10+ VP, or Conflict Deck empty → Endgame Intrigue cards → most VP wins. Ties: spice → Solari → water → garrisoned troops → most recent Reveal turn.

**Starting deck (10):** Convincing Argument x2, Dagger x2, Dune the Desert Planet x2, Diplomacy, Reconnaissance, Seek Allies, Signet Ring.

### Phase 2: Player Turns
Starting with the holder of the First Player marker and continuing clockwise, players take **one turn at a time**. On your turn, take either an **Agent turn** or a **Reveal turn**. Generally you take Agent turns until you run out of Agents, then take a Reveal turn — but Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left. Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase; the phase ends when all players have taken a Reveal turn.

You may play Plot Intrigue cards during this phase, at any point during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

**Agent turn** — play one card from your hand face up, using it to send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied board space:
- The board space must show (in its upper-left corner) an icon matching one of the Agent icons on the card. You must choose only one Agent icon on the card; one card can't send multiple Agents. A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn — it can only be revealed during a Reveal turn.
- You can't send an Agent to a board space that already has an Agent on it.
- You must pay any costs and meet any requirements of the space. Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card; if you can't pay, you can't send your Agent there.
- Gain the effects of the board space, the card's **Agent box**, and the one-space Influence advancement for a Faction space **in any order**, after paying the entry cost (ignore the card's Reveal box).
- Arrows mean cost (left of / above the arrow) then effect (right of / below it). An optional arrow effect can be paid and resolved **once**, never repeated by paying again. You may decline the payment and its effect on an ordinary card; board entry costs must be paid to enter, and an Intrigue card's costs and conditions must be met to play it. Most other board/card effects are mandatory unless they say “may,” use an optional arrow, or use the optional black-X trash icon. A non-arrow instruction to trash the card itself is mandatory.
- **Recruiting:** each troop icon recruits one troop — take it from your supply and place it in your garrison. (If your supply is out of troops, you can't recruit more until some return.)
- **Deploying:** troops sitting in your garrison can't earn rewards. Only when you send an Agent to a **Combat space** may you deploy troops to the Conflict area (the center of the garrisons): any or all troops you recruited this turn (from any source, including the board space, played card and Intrigue cards), **plus up to two more troops from your garrison**. You cannot re-recruit garrison troops to evade that limit. Recruited troops you don't deploy go to your garrison as usual.

**Reveal turn** — taken when you have no Agents left (or choose not to use remaining Agents). Four steps, in order:
1. **Reveal Cards:** reveal all cards remaining in your hand, face up, kept separate from cards you played on Agent turns.
2. **Resolve Reveal Effects:** gain the effects in the **Reveal boxes** of the cards you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round), in any order. A card drawn during your Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used in that turn; it cannot become an Agent turn. Cards drawn after your Reveal turn stay in your hand for next round, when you still draw five additional cards. You may spend Persuasion to acquire new cards before, between, or after your Reveal effects (see Actions).
3. **Set Strength:** total your strength for this round's Combat — each of your troops in the Conflict is worth **2 strength**; each sword you revealed during your Reveal turn is worth **1 strength**. Troops in your garrison or supply contribute nothing. You must have at least one troop in the Conflict to have any strength: if your last troop is ever removed, your strength becomes 0 and can't be increased by any means, including swords. Announce your total and move your Combat marker to that space of the Combat track (if over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track).
4. **Clean Up:** put all the cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) into your discard pile.

Note: a Reveal turn has no troop-deployment step. Deployment happens on Agent turns at Combat spaces (or via specific card/Control effects).

### Phase 3: Combat
- **Combat Intrigue cards:** starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player **with at least one troop in the Conflict** may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards, or pass. You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase. Once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, resolve the Combat. If a card changes a player's troops in the Conflict (or otherwise alters strength), adjust their Combat marker — remember, with no troops in the Conflict your strength is 0. A few Combat Intrigue cards trigger "when you win a Conflict": play those only after you've won, before moving to the next phase.
- **Resolve Combat:** rewards from the Conflict card are given by strength as shown on the Combat track. Highest strength wins the Conflict and gains the top reward; second-highest gains the second reward; **in a 4-player game only**, an ordinary third-place finisher gains the third reward. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
- **Ties:** tied for first place — no one wins the Conflict; each tied player receives the **second** reward (in a 4-player game, if two players tie for first, the other two still compete for the third reward). Tied for second — each receives the third reward, **including in two- and three-player games**; this differs from an ordinary third-place finish. Tied for third — nothing. “When you win a Conflict” effects cannot be used on a first-place tie because nobody won. If a win-trigger Intrigue is itself drawn as a victory reward, you may play it immediately.
- Once all rewards are given, each player takes their troops from the Conflict and puts them in their **supply (not their garrison)**. Reset all Combat markers to 0.

### Phase 4: Makers
Check each of the three board spaces with a Maker icon: The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin. If a space has no Agent on it, place 1 spice from the bank on it as bonus spice, adding to any bonus spice already accumulated there from previous rounds.

### Phase 5: Recall
- If any player is at **10 or more Victory Points** on the Score track, or the **Conflict Deck is empty**, the Endgame is triggered (see Scoring / Victory Conditions).
- If no one has won, prepare the next round: return the Mentat to its designated space in the Landsraad (if it isn't already there); players recall their Agents, returning them to their Leaders; pass the First Player marker clockwise; begin a new round with Phase 1. At the start of the next round, the winner of Sort Through the Chaos takes the Mentat as its Conflict reward (official FAQ timing).

## Actions

### Agent icons
Seven Agent icons appear on cards and board spaces: **Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen, Landsraad, City, Spice Trade**. A card's icons determine where it can send your Agent — e.g., Sardaukar Legion's Emperor icon reaches either of the two Emperor spaces, while its Landsraad icon instead reaches one of the five Landsraad board spaces (the Mentat's designated space is in the Landsraad). Each Faction has one board space with a cost and one without.

### Board spaces
Sending an Agent to a Faction's space also gains 1 Influence with that Faction (included below).
